Cyclic Design and Thematic Resonance in Iliad Books 3 and 6

Bruce Heiden The Ohio State University, USA

The present discussion of Iliad books 3 and 6 builds upon several earlier analyses of thematic design in the Iliad. In an article published in 1996 ', I demonstrated that the Iliad appears to have been designed as a series of three movements, illustrated by the following diagram.

![](https://www.persee.fr/renderIllustrationThumbnail/gaia_1287-3349_2003_num_7_1_T1_0159_0000_1.png)

The first « movement » consists of books 1 through 8, the second of books 9 through 15, and the last of books 16 through 24. Books 1, 9, and 16 are thematically analogous, in that each is oriented around a decision of Achilles that has consequences for the entire plot of the Iliad. Since Book 1 of course begins the whole epic, this suggested the hypothesis that books 9 and 16 might also share with book 1 the characteristic of initiating a « movement » in a planned complete performance.
